text:
maya: Anyone seen this On Android 11 emulator (API 30) our retry from Authenticator sometimes drops the Authorization header after we refresh the token. Only on emulator, ~25-40% of attempts.

devin: Hmm. Are you returning a new Request from okhttp3.Authenticator.authenticate?

maya: Yes, code is basically:
```java
@Override
public Request authenticate(Route route, Response response) throws IOException {
  String newToken = tokenProvider.refreshSync();
  return response.request().newBuilder()
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer " + newToken)
    .build();
}
```
Server logs show some retried requests missing Authorization.

arjun: Does refreshSync() use the same OkHttpClient instance? That can deadlock or reuse dispatcher threads.
maya: We use a dedicated client for refresh calls. The refresh completes every time but the returned request still sometimes arrives to backend without the header.
devin: Any interceptors that might strip headers on follow-up? network vs application interceptors?
maya: Only a network interceptor that adds x-client-id. Nothing that removes Authorization. Also this only repros on emulator API 30 images; physical devices and API 31+ fine.
arjun: Try explicit removeHeader("Authorization").addHeader(...) to be safe. Also try building a totally new Request.Builder() (copying method/url/body) instead of response.request().newBuilder().
maya: We tried both. removeHeader helped a little. Building new Request reduced frequency but didn't eliminate it. If I disable connection pooling the issue disappears.
devin: That smells like connection reuse behavior. Is server using HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2?
maya: HTTP/1.1. Emulator seems to prefer reusing connection so follow-up request goes on same TCP session.
arjun: Could be emulator network stack bug with keepalive and forged follow-up streams. Maybe the runtime re-sends without updated headers in certain timing windows. Any difference if you do the token refresh async and start a brand new call instead of returning from authenticate?
maya: Yes — doing an async enqueue and issuing a new call is stable. Not ideal because okhttp's built-in retry flow is nicer, but suggests a timing/connection-level race.
devin: Practical SDK steps: 1) For API <=30 emulator detection, add Connection: close on the retried request or set a header to force new connection for the follow-up. 2) Add DX note in onboarding docs about flaky emulator auth retries. 3) Open repro issue with OkHttp and Android emulator team.
maya: I put a small repro app together (native OkHttp 4.9.3) and tested: emulator API 30 consistent; API 31+ and physical hardware not affected. Filed issue upstream and created PR in our SDK that adds `.header("Connection", "close")` to the retried request when we detect emulator API 30. Marked with TODO to remove when upstream fixes.

ci-bot: CI: build passed on branch fix/emulator-auth-header. Tests: unit + small integration. :white_check_mark:

devin: Nice. Can you also add an automated e2e that runs the reproducer on a cloud emulator matrix (if infra supports API 30 images) so we don't regress?
maya: Yep, adding test + entry in devex known-issues doc. Thanks for the help :thumbsup:
